habits.habits: The torn-edge receipt card with a red circular 'stamp' appears twice (Moa and Tandem). All three use the same pale gray or white ground, a black pill primary button next to an outline secondary, and a small gray fine-print line under the CTAs. Pennywise uses pastel bento stat tiles. The Moa and Tandem heroes share the same left-text, right-card split. Small monospace timestamps and amounts recur.

All three pair a hero with a product UI mock and put a small fine-print reassurance line next to the CTA. The thin top nav with an outlined or underlined right-side link is the same everywhere. Otherwise the three differ clearly: a centered Korean hero over a ledger with a stacked bar, a left-aligned sans hero over a full app screenshot with an orange CTA, and a dark green full-bleed hero with a serif headline and a progress-bar card. Each has its own palette and type.

Monospace numbers and labels appear in all three. Tandem has torn receipt cards and Pennywise has pastel bento tiles. Moa has a framed panel with corner dots and a dark data board. A black primary button with a light secondary sits at the same scale throughout, and the fine-print reassurance row repeats. The headlines have some variety: number-led, itemised, and centered.

The hero splits text against a product card on two sites, and the fine-print trust row with free-trial microcopy repeats. All three use the same bordered or ruled data card with timestamped rows. Beyond that the sites are strongly different. Pennywise is a dark green-black page with a mint CTA and a table. Moa uses a sage ground, a red pill CTA and a heavy Korean display face. Tandem has a cobalt ground, a serif headline, a yellow CTA and the card placed on the left.

The torn receipt with a red circular stamp returns on Moa. A gray textured background with corner-dot frame marks is used on two sites. A dark mono 'terminal' board, pastel bento tiles on Pennywise, black pill buttons with a light secondary, and a fine-print reassurance line under the CTAs all repeat. Every hero is a large headline over a framed product artifact, and the logo strip uses the same treatment.

All three are white pages with a big headline, a black or single-accent CTA, and then a thin-bordered data table or timeline with a heavy top rule and small gray column headers. The table structure is nearly identical across finance-KR, finance-EN and SaaS. Each page uses one accent color sparingly, has the same fine-print line under the CTA, and uses an underlined text link as its secondary action. Only the headline typeface changes (serif, wide grotesk, Korean serif), so the layout and data-panel template is the same all three times.

All-white pages with near-black buttons. Every hero is a big headline over a hairline-ruled data table in a thin-bordered box. Each has a small gray meta line under the CTA. Product data is used as the hero image every time. Color is almost absent; only the type family changes (serif, wide grotesk, Korean serif).

Gray, faintly ribbed or textured backgrounds. Dark primary button next to a light pill ghost button. Monospace numbers in two sites (fee receipts, terminal-style clock). Receipt cards with zigzag edges and a red rubber stamp. A footer row of trust chips or logos. Pennywise breaks the pattern with a bright orange, mint and lilac bento grid.

Each site has its own color world (navy and yellow with a serif, sage with a red pill and heavy Korean display type, dark charcoal with mint). Shared habits: a headline-and-product-mockup split or stacked hero, a solid primary next to an outlined 'See how it works' button, a small meta line under the CTAs, and a card showing real product data.

Monospace numerals in orange on a dark panel and on receipt slips. Gray ribbed texture behind the Moa hero. Receipt cards with zigzag edges (Tandem). Black pill primary next to a gray pill secondary. A bento of colored rounded tiles (Pennywise). Every site shows its product data right under the headline.

A headline with a subline, a solid colored CTA (green, orange, mustard) and a text-link secondary. Every hero is followed by a bordered product-mockup card showing real data and progress bars. Footer strip of trust or logo text. Thin 1px rules throughout. Moa and Tandem share nearly the same white layout; Pennywise differs with deep green and a serif.

Receipt metaphor used twice (zigzag paper edge, round red 'DECIDED' and 0-won stamps, monospace amounts). Light gray background with an offset white paper card. Black primary next to an outlined secondary. Gray microcopy under the CTAs. The Pennywise orange, lilac and mint bento repeats from other sets. Headline left and paper card right in two of the three sites.

lost.text: Neither is weaker on direction: the two share an identical first screen and the same editorial serif plus ledger-table look built around Pennywise's left-to-spend budget, and the full pages differ only in pricing-table wording, where Y spells out "Not included" instead of a bare dash and names the plan in its button ("Try Plus free for 30 days"), which is why Y ships.

Neither version is weaker on direction: they share the same editorial serif, ledger-style budget table and plain black-and-white palette, and differ only in small pricing-table details. Y's bare dashes for features Basic lacks are less clear than X's explicit 'Not included'.

The two screenshots match except for the async-standups section, where X uses a generic stack of quoted lines and even puts quotation marks around names like "Priya Shah · Lisbon", while Y turns the updates into city-tagged cards with teal rules and an orange rule for the blocked one, carrying over the hero's time-zone timeline look.

In Y, the async-standups section loses X's row of teammate standup cards with their city labels and blocked-status accents, and turns them into a list of quoted names that copies the pain-point section above, so the page's main time-zone product artifact becomes generic text.

Both share the same passbook-ledger serif direction, but X breaks the '입출금·예적금' label onto two lines in the hero table and uses a generic '무료로 시작하기' CTA, while Y keeps the label on one line and uses a CTA specific to the product, '앱 받고 1분 만에 연결하기'.

Y uses a generic "무료로 시작하기" CTA instead of X's product-specific "앱 받고 1분 만에 연결하기", and its hero ledger wraps "입출금·예적금" onto two lines, which breaks the clean passbook-row rhythm the concept depends on.
X uses the same serif-and-ledger look, but its overspend nudge is just a red status line instead of a row you can act on ("Move $14"), so it shows less of what the product actually does.
Y squeezes the product's nudge into a cramped red status cell and drops the header CTA and trust line, so the ledger reads more like a generic table than a budgeting coach that suggests a next move.

X is missing a brand mark, and its timeline bars don't line up with their local times (Jonah's 07:40 update starts at 06). That weakens the page's one idea, mapping updates across time zones, which Y gets right and backs with the logo and the highlighted 'is blocked'.

Y drops the interlocking-rings logo mark and the orange 'is blocked' highlight, and its update bars no longer start at each teammate's posted local time, so the time-zone timeline feels more generic and less tied to Tandem's 'no 6am call' story.

Neither is weaker on direction: both use the same passbook-ledger concept, serif headline and monochrome table, so the gap is only in polish, where Y adds a header download button, a more specific call to action and a trust line, though its ledger runs past the first screen.

Y drops the MyData/no-fee trust line and the transfer and alert rows inside the ledger, so its bankbook gets more generic, though it frames the whole ledger neatly within the first screen, which X's cut-off table doesn't.

X shows a plain category table with no per-category progress bars, so the hero mockup reads like a generic spreadsheet rather than this app's own envelope-style budget view, and its "before November starts" headline contradicts the in-progress November budget shown right below it.

Y removes the per-category spend bars that made the hero's budget table read as a budgeting tool, so its type and palette could belong to any dark fintech; it also says 'before November starts' when the page shows it is already November, and a white band cuts off the bottom of the first screen.

X has the same navy, yellow and serif look, but it has no logo mark and its decision card has no 'agreed async by Design, Eng & PM' line or orange 'blocked' highlight, so less of it is tied to Tandem's async-decision story.

Y drops the interlocking-rings Tandem mark, the 'agreed async by Design, Eng & PM' decision line, the orange 'blocked' accent and the 'nobody has to be online at the same time' promise, and those were the details that tied the look to this async-collaboration brand, so it reads as a generic navy SaaS hero (it also loses the Sign in link and the customer trust strip).

Both versions share the same art direction: the heavy Korean display headline, the sage background, the red 0원 accent and the fee-comparison transfer card, so neither has weaker direction; Y is the better ship because it adds navigation and a reassurance line under the CTA, while X has no nav.

Neither is weaker: both use the same Moa layout, with the heavy display headline, the sage and vermilion palette, and the fee-comparison receipt card. Y drops the nav and the sign-up reassurance line, which costs usability but leaves the art direction unchanged.

Neither version is weaker: X and Y are byte-identical files (same MD5 hashes for the fold and full-page shots), so both have the same Tandem-specific direction, with a timezone-stamped async log, decision cards and navy-and-yellow serif branding.

Neither version is weaker: X and Y are byte-identical files (same checksums for both the fold and full-page shots), so they share the same Tandem-specific direction, built around the time-zone standup log, the decision record and the 'give your team its mornings back' framing.

X leaves its Zero-based budgets and Gentle nudges cards as empty colored tiles instead of mini product UI, so those cards lose the budgeting-specific feel. It also centers the dashboard tile text, which looks more like a generic template, and the stray capital 'Eating' in the headline is a polish error.

Y leaves out the product's own mini-interfaces: its Zero-based budgets and Gentle nudges cards are empty, its centered dashboard tiles look generic, and its headline has a stray capital in "Eating", so it reads less like Pennywise's actual app.

X drops the printed-receipt motif in the 'Also in the workspace' section and falls back to a generic two-column feature list, while Y presents it as an itemised receipt and gives the customer logos their own row, carrying the 'standup already printed' idea further down the page.

Y turns the 'Also in the workspace' itemised receipt into a plain two-column feature grid and shrinks the customer logos into a line of text, which weakens the printed-receipt idea that makes the page belong to Tandem.

X drops the receipt motif in its middle sections, so the transfer-fee and security bands fall back to generic white-band text lists, while Y carries the torn-paper fee receipt through the 0원 transfer section and an alternating steps layout.

Y drops the receipt for the 0원 transfer-fee section, so the page's key fee claim ends up as a plain white band of lists, and the receipt metaphor that makes the brand ownable starts to fade halfway down.

Y uses the same orange, lilac and black tile system, but its long, clumsy three-line headline pushes the budget tiles below the fold and crops them, so the page's most distinctive element, the live 'left to spend' dashboard, loses its impact.

Y uses the same orange, lilac and black card system, but its headline 'every dollar has a job' is a stock budgeting line any rival could use, and it drops X's '$14 over eating out' hook that ties the headline to the dashboard cards below.

Y swaps X's 'one digest for each person's morning' copy for a generic 'specs, decisions, roadmaps and standups live in one place' line and adds a stock AI-summaries teaser and logo strip, which weakens the printed-overnight-receipt idea that makes the page belong to Tandem.

Y drops the receipt motifs that carry past the hero card in X (the dashed perforation rule under the nav, the logo mark, the richer 'agreed async by Design, Eng & PM' detail), so the receipt idea sits only inside one card and not across the page.

X uses the receipt idea only for the hero card; Y also carries it into the dashed rule under the nav, the brand name in the headline and the 'like one receipt' section copy, and X's cramped, crooked stamp and missing trust line make it feel less finished.

Y uses the receipt idea less fully: it drops the dashed perforated rule under the nav and the monospace quantity columns, and its stamp is cramped and sits on top of the double rule, so it looks like a stuck-on badge instead of part of the receipt.

X has the same hero and bento palette, but further down the layout falls apart into generic rows: an uneven two-column list of extra features, step rows that run across with big empty gaps, and a closing CTA that only says "Compare Basic and Plus"; Y keeps the rounded money-card style all the way down the page.

Y uses the same Pennywise palette and money-figure type, but further down the page it drifts into generic layouts: plain numbered rows for the steps, a lopsided feature list, pricing cards that leave the right side of the row empty, and a weaker 'Compare Basic and Plus' closing button, so it loses the dashboard-tile language X carries all the way down.

X carries the receipt motif through only two hero slips and fills the third slot with a loose text link, so its 'itemised night' story reads as an unfinished collage rather than the full spec-and-roadmap tally that Y shows.

Y swaps the third receipt in the hero for a plain-text 'New: async standups' link, so the row of torn-paper receipts no longer reads as a complete set and the hero ends on generic SaaS announcement copy.

Y squeezes the features into a uniform three-column grid with a cramped first card and a stretched leftover '모으기' strip, so it loses X's deliberate staggered bento rhythm of dark ledger panels; its one gain is the dark '0원' fee highlight.

Y turns the Moa fee row into a plain table line instead of X's dark amber '0원' panel, and its evenly gridded feature cards drop the ledger-style emphasis that ties the page to this fee-free asset app.

X's overspend card shows '$14 over' as small caption text when every other tile uses an oversized figure, so the moment that shows Pennywise's warning feature reads like a generic notification instead of part of the brand's type system.

Y's direction is a little weaker because its dark Eating-out card drops the large '$14 over' figure; that card then reads as a generic notification row and breaks the big-number visual language used on every other tile.

Y folds the decision into a line in the standup list and drops the tilted decision receipt with its red APPROVED stamp, which weakens the 'itemised night' receipt idea and makes the cards read as generic dashboard panels.

X uses the receipt look only as styling on generic status cards; it has no approval stamp, tallied blocker count or dedicated decision receipt, so the 'itemised night' idea doesn't carry the page the way it does in Y.

X uses the brushed-metal, screwed-on instrument panel only as a frame around the dashboard, and its tick ruler has no numbers, so it reads as decoration rather than the meter-like identity Y builds by putting the whole hero on the plate and labelling the scale with asset proportions.

Y turns X's labeled asset-mix gauge into an unlabeled tick strip with no markers or caption, drops the 포인트·기타 row and the trust line under the buttons, so its instrument-panel look reads as decoration rather than a working dashboard for this money app.

Neither is weaker on direction: both use the same forest-green and gold palette, the same serif headlines and the same 'can see, never move' savings-goals story; X differs only in execution, with its trust strip pushed against the left edge of the screen.

The two share the same art direction (deep green, cream serif headlines, mustard accents, real savings-goal UI), so neither loses anything distinctive; Y is weaker on polish, with a trust strip that runs off the left edge, a duplicate savings-goals row, a 'someday' section with no body copy and a final CTA pushed out of alignment.

Both share the same Tandem-specific direction (time-zone stamps, standup and decision mockups, burnt-orange accents), so neither is weaker; Y simply ships better with a secondary 'See how it works' link in the hero and legible standup names in the sync section, where X fades them to a washed-out gray.

The two share the same direction: Tandem's time-zone standup story, the orange-on-ink palette and the product mock with city timestamps; Y differs only in execution, dropping the hero's 'See how it works' link and greying out the teammate names in the 'Stay in sync' section, which makes them harder to read.

Y is nearly identical but drops the '첫 계좌 연결까지 1분' note from the steps section, centres the FAQ so it breaks the page's left-heading two-column layout, and squeezes the two-line '모아에서 모아 보세요' wordplay closer onto one line, which blunts the brand's most distinctive moments.

Neither version is weaker on direction: both have the same Moa identity, with a heavy display Korean headline, green-and-gold asset ledger, ₩0 fee comparison and a dark security band, so the only differences are in layout polish, where Y's left-aligned two-column FAQ and stacked closing CTA hold the page grid better than X's narrow centered FAQ.

Neither is weaker on direction, since both use the same deep-green and cream palette, serif headline and savings-goal card, but X's hero copy is misaligned with the logo's left edge and it has no trust strip, so its read-only, security-first positioning looks less finished.

Y uses the same palette, serif type and savings-goals card but drops the hero's proof strip (read-only bank access, 256-bit encryption, never sells your data), which backed up the 'can see your money, can never move it' promise; Y also misaligns its hero text with the logo and the next section's heading.

X uses the same type, palette and product mock, but it doesn't push the client's 'eight time zones apart' idea. Its headline is a generic list of features, the city and local time sit as grey footnotes instead of accented stamps on each teammate, and the mock never shows the async decision being made, so the hero could belong to any team-workspace rival.

Y removes the details that tie the page to Tandem: the orange local timestamps beside each teammate, the logged decision row and the URL breadcrumb. What's left is a generic workspace mockup, Y has no sign-in link, and there's an empty gap at the bottom of its standup panel.

Neither version has weaker art direction: both use the same heavy display Korean headline, the same restrained green palette and the same ledger-style asset breakdown, so the only differences are in polish, where X has a stray rule running past the card, a cramped mock sidebar and the dashboard cut off at the fold, while Y lays out the summary as tidy label-and-value rows with more room.

X shows the same dashboard as a plain summary table and states the coverage only as "금융기관 350곳", while Y names 은행·카드·증권 in the headline and turns the preview into a 모아 ledger app with a 자산 원장/송금 sidebar.

Both use the same Pennywise look: an orange 'left to spend' hero card, mint and lilac budget tiles and heavy rounded numerals, so neither has weaker direction; X falls short on execution instead, with numbers and labels that wrap badly in the goal cards, a '$5 / month, billed yearly' price that breaks across lines, and uneven list spacing in the pricing cards, all of which Y fixes.

Neither version has weaker direction, since both use the same Pennywise look (orange, mint and lilac budget cards, heavy grotesk type, a dark closing band); Y loses only on polish, with '$1,080 /' and '$5 / month, billed yearly' wrapping badly and uneven bullet spacing in the Basic plan.

X uses the same timezone-console look but leaves the first feature card's lower half empty, where Y puts a city-by-city 'Blocked right now' roster, and it has no amber status dot on the hero's blocked count and no highlighted 'Most popular' Team pricing column, so its distributed-team story feels less finished.

Y drops the small amber signal touches that make the page feel like a live status board, such as the blocked-status dot, the 'blocked right now' teammate list in the async card and the highlighted 'Most popular' Team pricing column, so it reads as a more generic SaaS layout.

X uses the receipt motif in the hero and asset card but drops it in the transfer section, where a plain white bar and generic three-column text stand in for the itemized '수수료 0원' slip Y shows, so lower sections fall back to stock fintech layouts any rival could use.

In Y's send section, the torn-paper receipt card becomes a generic flat banner, so the receipt motif, the one idea that tied the page to Moa's zero-fee pitch, is weaker. Y's hero receipts also sit a little inside the page grid instead of lining up with its edges.

Y's direction is weaker: it swaps X's specific 'five minutes a week tells every dollar where to go' promise and its tighter, more composed bento of budget tiles for a looser layout and generic trust pills that any finance app could carry.

Y uses the same bento of orange, mint and lilac cards but drops the 'every penny' line that ties the headline to the Pennywise name, so its 'tell every dollar where to go' copy could belong to any budgeting app.

X shares the same timezone headline and departure-board standup panel but leaves the headline floating outside the riveted plate and uses a broken placeholder logo glyph, so the hardware look reads as a demo widget rather than the brand's own system.

Y loses the interlocking Tandem logo mark (it renders as a stray chevron) and cuts the 'nobody has to be online at the same time' and 'Agreed async' copy, so the page says less about async work across time zones and could belong to any workspace tool.

Y uses the same receipt concept but with less conviction: its stamp sits in empty space instead of being pressed onto the totals, and it drops the personal '민수님께 30,000원' line, so its Moa receipt reads like a tidy fee table rather than a real transfer slip.

X's Moa receipt is just the same fee math as the rival cards, with a stamp sitting in empty white space, while Y's shows a real transfer line ('민수님께 30,000원') and stamps it like an actual payment receipt.
